Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike — reserved throughput not being honored

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing worsening tail latency and a burst of 5xx errors hitting our checkout inference path at ~08:40 PDT. That coincides with a sustained increase in QPS from our end (we're within the committed monthly throughput), yet the Redwood Dedicated pool serving our reservation is showing queue depth and token queueing. Our telemetry (attached) indicates requests are being enqueued for several hundred ms and some requests are failing with 503s.

This is impacting user transactions; we've had a ~2% checkout abandonment in a 20-minute window. We need immediate mitigation and a clear timeline for corrective action. Our contract SOW and SLA (annex attached) expects the reserved throughput to be available for our peak windows.

Could you confirm receipt and tell us the mitigation steps you can enable right away? If this requires more capacity or temporary fallback, we need to understand options and any potential credits for the outage window.

Thanks,
Sasha Morales
Head of Engineering, ClearBridge

Quick technical summary (initial triage):
- Observed behavior: the dedicated pool's slot allocation stopped scaling at 09:05 PDT despite sustained enqueue depth. Autoscaler logs show repeated kernel selection failures on one host rack (NVLink peer fault) and a fallback to fewer instances, which reduced effective QPS capacity by ~25%.
- Impact: increased queueing and token wait leading to tail latencies and a subset of requests hitting the timeout path returning 503.
- Immediate mitigations we can enact (~10–25 minutes):
  1) Bypass the damaged rack: we can evacuate models from the affected nodes and shift ClearBridge's slices to healthy hosts in the same AZ (manual orchestration) — requires ops action and a brief rolling restart of slice containers (~8–12 min).
  2) Enable cross-tier fallback routing to Hosted API for non-sensitive traffics for up to 1 hour (rate-limited). This will require sales/leadership sign-off to authorize burst billing and potential data handling note (customer consent ok per prior agreement).
  3) If leadership authorizes, we can provision two additional reserved instances into the customer's pool (manual reserve for 24–72 hours) to cover the peak while hardware replacement/repair occurs — procurement/finance approval needed for the cost.
- Short-term ask: Jonas/ops to start evacuating the affected nodes and warm KV caches on target hosts. I will prepare a rollback plan and monitor the token queue metrics.
- Medium-term: schedule hardware replacement and add automated degraded-path escalation to avoid autoscaler kernel-failure stalls.

I'll monitor; tagging INF-4521 (runbook).

Rishi
Head of Inference Ops

- In-flight: cross-tier fallback toggle is ready but gated. If Sales/Finance approves temporary burst, we can route up to 25% of traffic to Hosted within 5 minutes and keep the remainder on Dedicated. This will remove pressure from the pool while repair completes.

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for raising this and for your patience. Quick summary of what we did and what comes next:

What we observed: your team hit a transient burst that exposed a hardware failure in a rack serving a slice of your Dedicated pool, which reduced effective capacity and caused queueing and a short window of 5xxs.

Immediate mitigations we executed (completed):
- Evacuated affected nodes and shifted your slices to healthy hosts in the same AZ (Jonas, Rishi).
- Warmed KV caches and increased prefetch to reduce cold-token latency.
- Reduced 5xx rate from ~1.9% to ~0.2% and restored tail latencies to within SLO for the current traffic shape.
- Prepared and staged Hosted fallback to allow up to 25% routing if you prefer an immediate offload while we finish hardware repairs.

Proposed next steps:
1) We recommend allowing Hosted fallback for up to 1 hour as a safety valve while our field team replaces the faulty rack. If you approve, we will enable it immediately (there will be short-lived cross-tier billing for any tokens served on Hosted).
2) Redwood will issue a pro-rated service credit for the 18-minute window of impact. I will follow up with Legal/Finance to finalize the credit calculation and paperwork.
3) We'll schedule a post-incident call with Rishi's team to review root cause and long-term mitigations (automated degraded-path escalation + additional headroom).

Please let me know if you want us to enable the Hosted fallback now. Apologies again for the disruption — we know this is critical to your customers.

Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
